$comment: Divergences between docs/plan/rls-policy-matrix.md and the schema that are deliberate. check_rls_matrix.py refuses to pass on anything not either fixed or listed here, and warns when a waiver stops matching anything -- a waiver for something that no longer diverges is its own small lie. Every entry needs a reason a stranger can evaluate, not just an id.

waivers.reason: Renamed. The matrix's `get_document_url(upload_ref, reason_code)` is `public.request_document_access`, which does exactly what the matrix describes including writing `audit.kyc_access` before any URL exists. The matrix text is stale, not the schema.
waivers.action: Rename in the matrix at the next edit of that section.

waivers.reason: Renamed. The matrix itself writes it as `get_my_verification() / get_my_kyc_profile()`; the second name is the one that shipped.
waivers.action: Drop the old name from the matrix.

waivers.reason: Split. `get_wallet()` became `public.my_balances()` plus `public.available_balance()`, because a balance and what is spendable from it are different questions -- `available_balance` subtracts referral commissions that are posted but still holding.
waivers.action: Update the matrix row to name both.

waivers.reason: Renamed. `attribute_referral(code)` shipped as `public.claim_referral_code`, with the same before-first-job rule the matrix states.

Renamed and split per surface: kyc_review_queue, dispute_queue, fraud_queue, moderation_queue, ticket_queue, business_verification_queue, config_change_queue. The matrix's generic `review_queue()` never existed as one function.
waivers.action: Replace the generic name in the matrix with the list.

waivers.reason: Not a client function. Name enquiry happens gateway-side in payments-worker and the result comes back through gateway_record_account_verification; `add_payout_account` is the client's half. Exposing a name-resolution endpoint to clients would be an account-enumeration oracle.
waivers.action: Correct the matrix: this is a worker path, not a client one.

waivers.reason: Superseded by reading the payment row, which carries the whole breakdown as columns (job_amount_minor, float_minor, float_surcharge_minor, discount_minor, fee_minor, amount_minor) under the same RLS the matrix specifies. A function returning the same numbers would be a second source of truth for money.
waivers.action: Replace the matrix row with a pointer to the payments columns.

waivers.reason: Not built, and blocks nothing today: it belongs to `saved_places`, which is not built either. Recorded in AUDIT-2026-09-22c as an open item for before the first live country.
Not built. Saved addresses with an access note revealed to the assigned provider during an active job only. A product feature, not a policy gap; it has no backend because it has no screen yet.
waivers.action: Build before the first live country (AUDIT-2026-09-22c).

waivers.reason: Not built. Kimi's provider tools page has an availability editor on mock data, so this is a real gap between the app and the backend -- but it is a missing feature rather than a broken control, and it is filed for Kimi in HANDOFF.md so the two halves land together.
waivers.action: Build alongside Kimi's M9 wiring of the provider tools page.

waivers.reason: Not built as a table. Per-country category settings live in `countries.config` jsonb and in the country packs, which is where the go-live gap check reads them from. A separate table would be a second place for the same fact.
waivers.action: Correct the matrix to name countries.config.

waivers.reason: Not built as a separate table. Attribution is `referrals` plus `referral_commissions`; the UNIQUE on one referrer per referee is what makes single-level structural, and a third table would let those disagree.
Not built. Phase 7's model half needs Vertex AI and GCP billing (client action 1). The deterministic half shipped without it.

Deliberate, and narrower than it was. The matrix gives a participant `R:part (status, amount)`; the grant is wider because a provider legitimately needs the amount breakdown that decides their own earnings, and a customer needs the fee and discount lines to understand what they paid. What was genuinely wrong -- `checkout_url`, which is a capability rather than a reference -- is revoked in 20260922121400_matrix_gaps.sql and moved behind `get_payment_checkout`, which checks the caller is the payer.
waivers.action: Correct the matrix cell to name the columns the product actually needs.

waivers.reason: Not a divergence. The matrix gives Support plain `R + F` on support_tickets -- they own the queue -- and the `R:scope` in that row belongs to the Dispute column, which the policy denies entirely. Narrower than specified, and fail-closed.
waivers.action: None. The heuristic reads the row, not the column.

waivers.reason: Narrower than specified, deliberately. The matrix gives Support `R:scope` on a user's notifications; the policy gives own-only and no admin clause at all. Reading somebody's notification history is the kind of blanket access S.1 was about, and support has the ticket thread for context.
waivers.action: Correct the matrix, or widen deliberately if support genuinely needs it.

waivers.reason: Narrower than specified. The matrix gives `R:part`, which would make read receipts possible; the policy gives own-only, so a 'seen' indicator has no backend. Fail-closed and harmless, but it is a product gap rather than a security one and the contract should not imply the feature works.
waivers.action: Decide whether read receipts ship. If they do, widen to participants; if not, correct the matrix.

waivers.reason: Not a divergence. The matrix cell is `R:part (own submissions)` and the policy tests `submitted_by = auth.uid()`, which is exactly that. The heuristic looks for participation helpers and does not recognise an ownership column as satisfying a narrowed R:part.
